The cost per volume was assumed to be $300/m3 which accounts for the quantity of the salt slurry required for a given energy capacity. The cost per surface area was assumed to be $3915/m2 and accounts for materials and manufacturing required for the tank shell. The assumed cost values were determined using the salt-only case (with an HTF hot temperature of 740°C) to establish a baseline cost of $22/kWh (SAM default value). The cost estimates do not consider the cost of the PCM particles. There is high uncertainty with these cost values, and future work should be conducted to reduce their uncertainty. In this work, we are focused more on the relative change rather than on the absolute values provided by the SAM model. To initialize the ETES model, we had to provide SAM the following information which is dependent on the HTF case: 1. HTF fluid properties table as a function of temperature. 2. sCO cycle performance as predicted by the Python design and off-design model. 2 3. sCO cycle and TES costs. 2 All other parameter values were held constant at their default value for each HTF case. The internal rate of return (IRR) estimate is based on an assumed power purchase agreement of $75/MWh with a 1% escalation and SAM default time-of-delivery hourly factors. This analysis was conducted with the energy arbitrage dispatch optimization model enabled. This dispatch approach targets low prices for charging and high prices for discharge to maximize system revenue subject to system operational constraints. This approach ensures that the ETES system operates only when it is profitable; however, the ETES predicted operations and IRR are specific to the time-of-delivery hourly factors used in this study.
